confusions: I did not know which page held the welfare figures, so I had to hunt through the long Questions list (about six screens) before finding 'How has welfare spending changed?' near the bottom.
The Spending page is about all public money, and I was not sure it would have benefits in it, so I went there first for nothing.
The welfare page has four measures (after inflation, per person, share of GDP, share of spending) and I could not tell which one a question wanted without reading the whole thing.
I did not understand the words 'welfare', 'social security', 'DWP benefit spending' and 'without pensions', and they seemed to mean different things on the same page.
The year-by-year page is very long with eight sections, so finding the class sizes and first-time buyer age took several taps and scrolls.
The house price page has a chart where the line breaks in 2008, and I did not know if the numbers either side could be compared.
I could not find the '0 to 9 months' detail for the state pension age answer on the page, so I had to pick the closest match.
The 10% deposit question needed a sum, and I was not sure the site had the answer until I found the 0.76 years line in the text.
I had to go back to the Questions list twice, and the back button did not always return me to where I had been.
